bio.en: Born into an extremely wealthy Catholic aristocratic family, he led the small anti-war faction in parliament that demanded an immediate peace during the First World War. The Aster Revolution of October 1918 made him prime minister; when the People’s Republic was proclaimed on 16 November he also became provisional head of state, and in January 1919 he was recognised as president. As an example for land reform he gave his family estates to his tenants. After his government fell over the Vix note in March 1919 the Soviet Republic was proclaimed, and in July he went into exile. He returned in 1946 and was ambassador to France from 1947 to 1949, resigning in protest at the Rajk trial, and died in Vence, France, in 1955.

bio.en: Raised in a Protestant family in Kiskunhalas, he worked as a bricklayer, joined the labour movement and in 1901 the Social Democratic Party, and led the building workers’ union and the Workers’ Insurance Fund. He backed the merger of the Social Democrats and Communists on 21 March 1919 and, as chairman of the Revolutionary Governing Council, became the Soviet Republic’s formal head of state and prime minister, though real power lay with Béla Kun. After the fall he was education minister in the Peidl government; captured by the Romanian army, he escaped from Cluj and lived in exile in Bratislava, Vienna and Paris. Refused permission to return after the war, he died in Paris in 1947.

bio.en: Born to a Jewish family in Nyíregyháza, he became a journalist and was taken prisoner by Russia during the First World War. After the October Revolution he organised Communist Hungarian prisoners of war in Moscow with Béla Kun, and in December 1918 he took part in founding the Spartacist League in Germany. In the Soviet Republic he was deputy people’s commissar of war and commissar of public education, and his guards became known as the Lenin Boys. A central figure of the Red Terror, which executed suspected counter-revolutionaries without trial, he flew to Moscow in late May to see Lenin. He died on 2 August 1919 after being caught crossing into Austria; the authorities reported that he had shot himself.

bio.en: Born to a Jewish family in Gelse, he became a lawyer and, as legal adviser to the railway workers’ federation, defended the leaders of the national railway strike in 1904. He joined the Social Democratic Party in 1908 and moved steadily left until he became a Communist. In March 1919 he agreed with Béla Kun in prison on introducing the dictatorship of the proletariat; in the Soviet Republic he was commissar for the interior and for trade, then commanded the Red Army’s III Corps in the northern campaign and became commander-in-chief in July. After the fall he emigrated to Austria and led the exiled Communist movement. He died in Cannes in 1928, and his ashes were placed in the Kremlin Wall.

In exile he lived in Vienna, Czechoslovakia and Sweden; he headed the Hungarian legation in Sweden from 1946 to 1948 and resigned when the Social Democrats were merged into the Communist Party. He died in Stockholm in 1949.

bio.ko: 너지카로이의 유대계 의사 집안에서 태어났고, 1881년 가족이 성을 야시로 바꾸고 개혁교회로 개종했다. 1900년 사회과학지 『후서디크 사저드』(20세기)를 함께 창간해 20년 동안 이끈 편집자가 되었고, 보통·비밀 선거권과 토지개혁을 주장했다. 1914년 6월 전국 시민급진당을 창당했다. 1918년 10월 과꽃 혁명 뒤 카로이 정부의 민족 담당 장관으로서 소수민족에게 최대한의 자치를 제시해 헝가리 국경 안에 붙잡아 두려 했으나 실패했고, 12월 사임했다. 평의회 공화국이 사상과 양심의 자유를 부정한다며 1919년 5월 1일 망명했다. 1925년 미국 오벌린 칼리지의 역사학 교수가 되어 『합스부르크 군주국의 해체』(1929)를 썼고, 1957년 오벌린에서 죽었다.
bio.en: Born to a Jewish doctor’s family in Nagykároly, he saw the family change its name to Jászi and convert to Calvinism in 1881. In 1900 he co-founded the social-science review Huszadik Század (Twentieth Century) and became its leading editor for two decades, arguing for universal secret suffrage and land reform. In June 1914 he founded the National Civic Radical Party. After the Aster Revolution of October 1918 he became minister of nationalities in the Károlyi government and tried to keep the minorities within Hungary by offering them maximum autonomy, but failed and resigned in December. Unable to tolerate the Soviet Republic’s denial of freedom of thought and conscience, he emigrated on 1 May 1919. In 1925 he joined the faculty of Oberlin College in the United States as a history professor, wrote The Dissolution of the Habsburg Monarchy (1929) and died in Oberlin in 1957.

bio.ko: 1875~1890년 총리를 지낸 티서 칼만의 아들로, 칼뱅파 하급 귀족 가문에서 자라 부다페스트와 하이델베르크, 베를린에서 공부했다. 1886년 자유당 의원으로 정계에 들어섰고, 1903~1905년과 1913~1917년 두 차례 헝가리 총리를 지냈으며 1912~1913년에는 하원의장이었다. 오스트리아와의 이중군주국 체제를 누구보다 열렬히 지지했고, 보통선거권과 대토지 분할에 반대했다. 1914년 7월 세르비아와의 전쟁에 처음에는 홀로 반대했으나 결국 지지로 돌아섰다. 개혁을 내건 카를 왕의 요구로 1917년 5월 사임했다. 1918년 10월 31일 과꽃 혁명 중 부다페스트의 집에 들이닥친 병사들에게 살해되었다.
bio.en: The son of Kálmán Tisza, prime minister from 1875 to 1890, he grew up in a Calvinist family of untitled lower nobility and studied in Budapest, Heidelberg and Berlin. He entered parliament for the Liberal Party in 1886, was prime minister of Hungary twice, in 1903–1905 and 1913–1917, and Speaker of the House in 1912–1913. The most zealous adherent of the Dual Monarchy with Austria, he opposed universal suffrage and the break-up of the great estates. In July 1914 he alone at first opposed war with Serbia, but in the end supported it. Asked to resign by the reforming King Charles, he stepped down in May 1917. On 31 October 1918, during the Aster Revolution, he was killed by soldiers who broke into his home in Budapest.

bio.ko: 코마롬 주의 개혁교회 집안에서 태어난 법률가로, 1918년까지 법무부 국제국장을 지냈고 사회과학지 『후서디크 사저드』의 창간 회원이었다. 과꽃 혁명 뒤 1918년 11월부터 카로이 정부의 법무장관을 지냈고, 1919년 1월 총리가 되었다. 3월 20일 프랑스의 페르낭 빅스 중령이 협상국 각서를 건네자 영토 보전을 해치는 조건을 받아들일 수 없다며 내각과 함께 사임했고, 이로써 평의회 공화국 수립의 길이 열렸다. 그 뒤 정계에서 물러나 1920년부터 변호사로 일하며 국제법·형법·민법에 관한 연구를 냈다. 1944년 부다페스트에서 심장마비로 죽었다.
bio.en: A lawyer from a Calvinist family in Komárom County, he headed the international department of the Ministry of Justice until 1918 and was a founding member of the social-science review Huszadik Század. After the Aster Revolution he was justice minister in the Károlyi government from November 1918 and became prime minister in January 1919. When the French Lieutenant Colonel Fernand Vix handed him the Entente note on 20 March, he resigned with his cabinet rather than accept terms that violated the country’s territorial integrity, opening the way to the Soviet Republic. He then withdrew from politics, worked as a lawyer from 1920 and published studies in international, criminal and private law. He died of a heart attack in Budapest in 1944.

bio.ko: 알자스 출신의 프랑스 직업 군인으로, 1898년 생시르 사관학교를 졸업하고 식민지 부대의 참모장교로 복무했다. 제1차 세계대전 말 베오그라드의 프랑스 동방군 사령부에 있던 그는 1918년 11월 26일 중령으로서 협상국 군사사절단장이 되어 부다페스트에 왔고, 파도바 휴전협정과 베오그라드 군사협정의 이행을 감시했다. 헝가리 정부에 여러 차례 철수 요구 각서를 전달했으며, 1919년 3월 20일 카로이 대통령에게 건넨 각서로 정부가 이튿날 사임했다. 평의회 공화국이 선포된 뒤 사절단은 괴롭힘을 받다가 3월 26일 기차로 세게드로 떠났다. 그 뒤 레반트 등지의 식민지 부대에서 복무해 1933년 사단장급 장군이 되었고, 1941년 뇌이쉬르센에서 죽었다.
bio.en: An Alsatian-born French professional soldier, he graduated from Saint-Cyr in 1898 and served as a staff officer of the colonial troops. At the end of the First World War he was on the staff of the French Army of the Orient in Belgrade, and on 26 November 1918 he arrived in Budapest as a lieutenant colonel at the head of the Entente military mission, charged with overseeing the Padua armistice and the Belgrade military convention. He passed several notes demanding withdrawals to the Hungarian government; the note he handed President Károlyi on 20 March 1919 brought the government down the next day. Harassed after the Soviet Republic was proclaimed, the mission left by train for Szeged on 26 March. He later served with colonial troops in the Levant and elsewhere, became a général de division in 1933 and died in Neuilly-sur-Seine in 1941.

bio.ko: 영국령 케이프 식민지의 아프리카너 집안에서 태어나 케임브리지에서 법학을 공부했다. 제2차 보어 전쟁에서 코만도 부대 장교로 싸웠고, 1902년 페레니힝 조약 협상에서 핵심 역할을 했다. 1910년 남아프리카 연방 창설을 이끌었고, 국방장관으로서 제1차 세계대전 동안 연방 방위군을 책임졌으며 1917년 영국 제국전시내각에 들어갔다. 1919년 파리 강화회의에서 국제연맹 창설을 주도했고, 4월 4일 부다페스트에 가서 쿤 벨러 정부에 빅스 각서보다 유리한 중립지대와 봉쇄 해제를 제시했으나 쿤이 거부하자 협상을 끝냈다. 1919~1924년과 1939~1948년 남아프리카 연방 총리를 지냈고 1941년 원수가 되었다. 1950년 심장마비로 죽었다.
bio.en: Born to Afrikaner parents in the British Cape Colony, he studied law at Cambridge. He fought as an officer in a commando unit in the Second Boer War and played a key role in negotiating the Treaty of Vereeniging in 1902. He led the creation of the Union of South Africa in 1910, was responsible as defence minister for the Union Defence Force in the First World War and joined the Imperial War Cabinet in London in 1917. At the Paris Peace Conference of 1919 he championed the League of Nations, and on 4 April he went to Budapest, offering Béla Kun’s government a neutral zone more favourable than the Vix note and the lifting of the blockade; when Kun rejected the terms he ended the talks. He was prime minister of the Union of South Africa in 1919–1924 and 1939–1948 and became a field marshal in 1941. He died of a heart attack in 1950.

bio.en: A physician turned journalist from the Vendée, he became mayor of the 18th arrondissement of Paris in 1870 and the next year tried to broker a compromise between the Paris Commune and the government. A key figure of the Independent Radicals, he advocated the separation of church and state. As interior minister in 1906 he ordered repressive policies toward the workers’ movement and was nicknamed “the Tiger”, and he was prime minister in 1906–1909 and 1917–1920. Appointed in November 1917 at one of the darkest hours of the war, he demanded total victory over Germany and achieved the Treaty of Versailles at the Paris Peace Conference. Seeking to weaken Hungary as Germany was weakened, he brought about the stringent terms of the Treaty of Trianon. He died in 1929.

bio.ko: 니르바크터의 오랜 귀족 가문에서 태어났고, 카로이 미하이의 사촌이다. 상원 의원이 되었고 1906~1910년 아라드 주지사를 지냈다. 1919년 5월 평의회 공화국에 맞서 아라드에서 반혁명 정부를 세웠으나 루마니아군에 억류되었고, 풀려난 뒤 5월 30일 프랑스군이 점령한 세게드에서 정부를 다시 꾸렸다. 이때 호르티 미클로시에게 국방장관으로서 국민군을 세워 달라고 청했고, 두 사람은 평생의 벗이 되었다. 1930~1931년 베틀렌 정부의 외무장관을 거쳐 1931년 8월 총리가 되었고, 비어토르바지 고가교 폭파 뒤 계엄을 선포해 공산주의자를 가두었다. 1932년 9월 사임했고, 1939년 제2차 유대인법에 항의해 모든 직위에서 물러났다. 1947년 부다페스트에서 죽었다.
bio.en: Born into an old aristocratic family in Nyírbakta, he was a first cousin of Mihály Károlyi. He entered the House of Magnates and was ispán of Arad County from 1906 to 1910. In May 1919 he formed a counter-revolutionary government against the Soviet Republic in Arad but was interned by the Romanians; after his release he reorganised it on 30 May in French-occupied Szeged, asking Miklós Horthy to set up the National Army as war minister, and the two became lifelong friends. After serving as foreign minister in Bethlen’s government in 1930–1931 he became prime minister in August 1931, and after the Biatorbágy viaduct bombing he imposed martial law and imprisoned Communists. He resigned in September 1932, and in 1939 he gave up all his posts in protest against the second Jewish law. He died in Budapest in 1947.

bio.ko: 우이페슈트의 독일계 개신교 지식인 집안에서 태어났다. 1896년 루도비커 사관학교를 졸업하고 빈 군사대학을 마쳤으며, 1913년 헝가리군 출신으로는 처음으로 빈 군사대학 교수가 되었다. 1919년 1월 사회민주당에 입당했고 국방차관으로 군 조직을 맡았다. 평의회 공화국 시기인 4월 21일 붉은군대 참모장이 되어 미슈콜츠 부근에서 승리하고 북부 원정을 이끌었으나, 7월 3일 클레망소 각서 수락과 철수 명령에 항의해 사임했다. 붕괴 뒤 체포되어 1920년 반역죄로 징역 3년을 선고받았고, 1925년부터 불법 공산당원이었다. 1927년 죽었고 1945년 사후 상급대장으로 추서되었다.
bio.en: Born in Újpest into a German-origin Evangelical family of intellectuals, he graduated from the Ludovika Academy in 1896, studied at the War Academy in Vienna and in 1913 became its first professor from the Hungarian army. In January 1919 he joined the Social Democratic Party and as state secretary was put in charge of army organisation. Under the Soviet Republic he became chief of staff of the Red Army on 21 April, won an important victory near Miskolc and led the northern campaign, but resigned on 3 July in protest at the acceptance of the Clemenceau note and the order to withdraw. Arrested after the fall, he was sentenced to three years for treason in 1920, and from 1925 he was a member of the illegal Communist Party. He died in 1927 and was posthumously promoted to colonel general in 1945.

bio.ko: 부다페스트의 노동자 가정에서 태어나 구두공으로 일하다 제1차 세계대전 때 오스트리아-헝가리 해군에서 복무했다. 1918년 소비에트 러시아로 탈출해 헝가리인 공산주의자 그룹에 들어가 선동가 학교에서 배웠다. 1918년 12월 귀국해 공산당 본부를 지키는 수병 경비대에 들어갔다. 평의회 공화국에서 200명이 넘는 무장대를 이끌며 혁명재판소의 재판도 맡았고, 그의 부하들은 반혁명 혐의자를 재판 없이 체포·고문·처형했다. 4월 말 뵘 빌모시의 해산 명령으로 무장해제되었으나 6월 봉기 뒤 쿤 벨러에게 재무장을 요청해 활동을 이어 갔다. 붕괴 뒤 8월 4일 체포되었고, 살인 9건으로 사형을 선고받아 1919년 12월 18일 교수형에 처해졌다.
bio.en: Born into a working-class family in Budapest, he worked as a shoemaker and served in the Austro-Hungarian Navy in the First World War. In 1918 he escaped to Soviet Russia, joined the Hungarian Communist group and studied at an agitators’ school. Back in Hungary by December 1918, he joined the sailor detachment guarding the Communist Party headquarters. Under the Soviet Republic he commanded more than two hundred men and oversaw some revolutionary tribunal trials, while his men arrested, tortured and executed suspected counter-revolutionaries without trial. Ordered to disarm by Vilmos Böhm at the end of April, the group was re-armed at his request to Béla Kun after the June rising and resumed its activities. Arrested on 4 August after the fall, he was convicted of nine murders and hanged on 18 December 1919.

bio.ko: 오늘날 슬로바키아의 말라츠키에서 독일계 약사 집안에 태어났다. 공학을 공부해 베를린 AEG에서 일한 뒤 부다페스트 근교에서 기계 공장을 운영했다. 1912년 카로이 미하이의 독립당에 들어가 그의 가까운 벗이 되었고, 과꽃 혁명 뒤 국방차관을 지냈으나 점차 우파로 기울어 1919년 2월 해임되었다. 평의회 공화국 때 체포되어 사형을 선고받았다가 감형되어 탈출했다. 1919년 8월 우익 단체 「백악관 동지회」와 함께 페이들 정부를 몰아냈고, 8월 7일 요제프 아우구스트 대공에 의해 총리로 임명되어 11월 24일까지 재임했다. 1951년 라코시 정권에 체포되어 징역 15년을 선고받고 그해 죽었으며, 1990년 복권되었다.
bio.en: Born into a pharmacist’s family of German origin in Malacka (now Malacky, Slovakia), he studied engineering, worked for AEG in Berlin and then ran his own machinery works outside Budapest. He joined Mihály Károlyi’s Independence Party in 1912 and became one of his closest friends; after the Aster Revolution he was state secretary for war, but he drifted to the right and was dismissed in February 1919. Arrested under the Soviet Republic and sentenced to death, he had the sentence commuted and escaped. In August 1919 he joined the right-wing White House Comrades’ Association in ousting the Peidl government; on 7 August he was named prime minister, with Archduke Joseph August as regent, and held office until 24 November. Arrested by Rákosi’s regime in 1951 and sentenced to fifteen years, he died the same year; he was rehabilitated in 1990.

bio.ko: 헝가리의 얼추트에서 합스부르크-로트링겐 가문의 헝가리(팔라틴) 분가에서 태어났다. 1890년 군에 들어가 제1차 세계대전에서 군단과 군, 집단군을 지휘했고, 1918년 10월 24일 오스트리아-헝가리군의 마지막 원수가 되었다. 10월 27일 카를 황제가 그를 헝가리의 전권 대리인(호모 레기우스)으로 삼았으나 과꽃 혁명으로 계획이 무산되었다. 평의회 공화국이 무너진 뒤 1919년 8월 카를을 대신하는 섭정으로서 국가원수가 되어 프리드리히 이슈트반을 총리로 임명했지만, 협상국이 합스부르크가의 국가원수를 인정하지 않아 8월 23일 물러났다. 호르티 시대에는 1936~1944년 헝가리 과학아카데미 원장을 지냈다. 1944년 헝가리를 떠났고 1962년 서독의 라인에서 죽었다.
bio.en: Born at Alcsút in Hungary into the Hungarian or Palatinal branch of the House of Habsburg-Lorraine, he entered the army in 1890, commanded a corps, an army and army groups in the First World War and on 24 October 1918 became the last field marshal of the Austro-Hungarian army. On 27 October Emperor Charles made him homo regius of Hungary, but the Aster Revolution put an end to his plans. After the fall of the Soviet Republic he became head of state in August 1919 as regent for Charles and appointed István Friedrich prime minister, but when it became clear that the Allies would not recognise a Habsburg as head of state he was forced to resign on 23 August. In the Horthy era he was president of the Hungarian Academy of Sciences from 1936 to 1944. He left Hungary in 1944 and died in Rain, West Germany, in 1962.

bio.ko: 님부르크에서 태어난 기계 조립공으로, 1895년 사회민주당에 들어갔고 1906년부터 노동자 언론인이자 노동단체 간부로 일했다. 1918년부터 부다페스트에 살며 클라드노의 신문 『스보보다』의 통신원으로 일했고, 1919년 헝가리 공산당 중앙위원회의 체코·슬로바키아 분과를 이끌었다. 헝가리 붉은군대가 슬로바키아로 진격한 뒤 프레쇼우에서 슬로바키아 평의회 공화국을 선포하고 혁명통치평의회 의장이 되었으나, 이 국가는 7월 7일 체코슬로바키아군이 헝가리군을 밀어내면서 사라졌다. 평의회 공화국 붕괴 뒤 헝가리에서 투옥되었다가 1920년 체코슬로바키아 당국에 넘겨졌다. 1922년 소련 시민권을 받고 소련으로 가서 국제노동자구호회 일을 맡았다. 1941년 자연사했다.
bio.en: Born in Nymburk, he was originally an engine fitter; he joined the Social Democratic Party in 1895 and from 1906 was a workers’ journalist and an official of workers’ associations. Living in Budapest from 1918 as a correspondent of the Kladno paper Svoboda, he led the Czech and Slovak section of the Hungarian Communist Party’s central committee in 1919. After the Hungarian Red Army entered Slovakia he proclaimed the Slovak Soviet Republic in Prešov and became chairman of its Revolutionary Governing Council, but the state ceased to exist on 7 July when Czechoslovak troops pushed the Hungarians out. Imprisoned in Hungary after the fall of the Hungarian Soviet Republic, he was handed over to the Czechoslovak authorities in 1920. Granted Soviet citizenship, he moved to Soviet Russia in 1922 and worked for International Workers’ Aid. He died of natural causes in 1941.

bio.ko: 트란실바니아의 오랜 귀족 가문 출신으로 1901년 자유주의자로 의회에 들어갔다. 1919년 세게드의 반혁명 세력에 합류했고, 1921년 4월 카를 왕의 첫 복귀 시도 뒤 총리가 되었다. 통일당을 세우고 1922년 선거법으로 농촌에 공개투표를 되살려 집권당의 승리를 굳혔으며, 사회민주당과 협정을 맺고 국제연맹 가입과 차관으로 경제를 안정시켰다. 1931년 대공황 속에 물러났고, 1941년 소련과의 전쟁에 반대했다. 1945년 소련군에 체포되어 1946년 모스크바의 감옥에서 죽었다.
bio.en: Scion of an old Transylvanian noble family, he entered parliament as a liberal in 1901. He joined the counter-revolution in Szeged in 1919 and became prime minister in April 1921, after King Charles’s first return attempt. He founded the Unity Party, secured its victories by restoring the open ballot in the countryside with the Franchise Act of 1922, concluded a pact with the Social Democrats, and stabilised the economy through League of Nations membership and a loan. He resigned in the Depression in 1931 and in 1941 opposed war with the Soviet Union. Arrested by the Soviets in 1945, he died in a Moscow prison in 1946.

bio.en: Born in Murga, Tolna County, the son of the village schoolmaster, he served as an Austro-Hungarian officer in the First World War. In Szeged in 1919 he founded the paramilitary MOVE and played a leading role in organising Horthy’s National Army, and in 1921 he led the armed opposition to King Charles’s return. He became defence minister in Bethlen’s government in 1929 and prime minister in 1932. He aligned with Mussolini, signing the Rome Protocols in 1934, and as the first foreign head of government to visit Hitler concluded a trade agreement with Germany. He died of illness in Munich in 1936.

bio.en: Born in Budapest to an aristocratic family from Transylvania, he was a geographer, university professor, member of the Academy of Sciences and chief scout of the Hungarian Scout Association. In 1918–19 he compiled the “Red map” of ethnic distribution based on the 1910 census. As foreign minister he attended the signing of the Treaty of Trianon in 1920, became prime minister in July and led the government of the numerus clausus period until April 1921. Prime minister again from 1939, he wrote the preamble to the Second Anti-Jewish Law and prepared the Third. He killed himself on 3 April 1941 when German troops were about to cross Hungary to invade Yugoslavia.

bio.en: Born to an old noble family in Romhány, Nógrád County, the career officer took command of Horthy’s bodyguard in Szeged in 1919 and formed the first officer detachment. Torturing and killing Communists, Social Democrats, peasants and Jews, his unit is considered the most brutal of the Hungarian White Terror. Convicted of extortion in 1921, he lost his command and joined King Charles’s second return attempt; his battalion was dissolved in January 1922. He failed to build a fascist mass movement in the 1930s and in October 1944 again assembled a squad to hunt Jews. Captured by Soviet troops in 1945, he died in the Gulag.

bio.en: A count born in Vienna, he entered parliament in 1877 and was a leading orator for half a century. As education minister in 1906–1910 he drafted the Apponyi laws of 1907, which imposed Hungarian-language teaching on non-Hungarian schools. He led the Hungarian delegation at the Paris peace talks in January 1920 and spoke on 16 January, without changing the terms, and in March lost the regency vote to Horthy. Thereafter, as a legitimist opposition deputy and Hungary’s representative at the League of Nations, he denounced the injustice of the Trianon borders. He died in Geneva in 1933, where he had come for the Disarmament Conference.

bio.ko: 에르되퓔레에서 태어났고 1916년까지 홀렌데르라는 성을 썼다. 금융기관 사무원으로 일하며 제1차 세계대전 중 코르빈 오토와 반군국주의 운동을 조직하다 1918년 체포되었다. 1919년 평의회 공화국에서 내무 인민위원부 정치부의 코르빈 대리를 지냈다. 공화국이 무너지자 빈을 거쳐 모스크바로 망명해 국제적색구원회 일을 했고, 쿤 벨러의 제안으로 귀국해 불법 당 출판을 맡았다. 1932년 7월 체포되어 비어토르바지 폭파와 무관함에도 사형을 선고받고 7월 29일 퓌르시트 샨도르와 함께 교수형에 처해졌다.
bio.en: Born in Erdőfüle, he bore the surname Hollender until 1916. A bank clerk, he organised an anti-militarist movement with Ottó Korvin during the First World War and was arrested in 1918. In the 1919 Soviet Republic he was Korvin’s deputy in the political department of the people’s commissariat of the interior. After its fall he fled via Vienna to Moscow and worked for International Red Aid, and was sent home on Béla Kun’s proposal to run the illegal party press. Arrested in July 1932, he was sentenced to death although he had no part in the Biatorbágy bombing, and was hanged with Sándor Fürst on 29 July.

Repeatedly arrested from 1928 and released for lack of evidence, he lost his job; in 1930 he joined the party leadership and was soon arrested again. In 1932, under the summary jurisdiction proclaimed after the Biatorbágy bombing, he was sentenced to death together with Imre Sallai. bio.en: A machinist from Városlőd in Veszprém County, he led the metalworkers’ and miners’ unions. He ran the mining sector under the Soviet Republic in 1919 and after its fall was interior minister in the Peidl government and minister of labour and welfare under Huszár. When the Social Democrats boycotted the election because of the terror, he resigned in January 1920 and fled to Austria. Back in 1921, he concluded the pact with Bethlen’s government; he was a deputy from 1922 to 1944 and from 1927 general secretary of the Trade Union Council. In 1944 he was held in Mauthausen. Opposing the post-war merger with the Communists, he was expelled in 1947, emigrated to the United States and died in New York in 1956.

bio.ko: 케치케메트의 부유한 농가에서 태어나 제1차 세계대전 말 오스트리아-헝가리 항공대의 전투기 조종사로 복무했다. 1919년 세게드에서 호르티의 참모장에게 케치케메트 일대의 「질서 회복」을 위임받아 도나우강·티서강 사이 지역의 사실상 군정관이 되었다. 그의 부대는 사람들을 오르고바니 숲으로 끌고 가 고문하고 처형했으며 이자크에서 포그롬을 일으켰고, 희생자의 약 3분의 1이 유대인이었다. 1921년 카를 왕의 복귀를 지지하지 않은 공으로 호르티의 사면을 받았고 1927~1931년 국회의원을 지냈다. 전후 궐석 재판에서 사형을 선고받았고 1950년 스페인 비고에서 병으로 죽었다.
bio.en: Born into a wealthy peasant family in Kecskemét, he was a fighter pilot in the Austro-Hungarian Aviation Troops by the end of the First World War. In Szeged in 1919 Horthy’s chief of staff ordered him to “make order” around Kecskemét, and he became the de facto military governor of the Danube–Tisza Interfluve. His men took abducted people to the forest of Orgovány to be tortured and executed and staged a pogrom at Izsák; about a third of their victims were Jewish. Because he did not back King Charles’s return in 1921, Horthy’s amnesty shielded him, and he sat in parliament from 1927 to 1931. After the war he was sentenced to death in absentia, and he died of illness in Vigo, Spain, in 1950.

bio.ko: 마로시바샤르헤이에서 태어난 장교로, 평의회 공화국이 무너진 뒤 쇼프론의 헌병 사령관이 되었다. 1920년 2월 17일 그의 장교 부대원들이 『네프서버』의 쇼모지 벨러와 버초 벨러를 살해해 호르티에 반대하는 세력에 경고를 보냈고, 3월 섭정 선거 때는 그의 부대가 국민의회의 「질서」를 지켰다. 1921년 8월 쇼프론 철수를 거부해 이 도시가 헝가리에 남을 길을 열었다. 같은 해 10월 왕정주의 장교들과 함께 카를 왕을 불러들여 장갑열차로 부다페스트로 진군했으나 부더외르시 전투에서 졌고, 사면을 받은 뒤 퇴역했다. 1932년 프로너이 팔과 함께 헝가리 전국 파시스트당을 세웠다.
bio.en: Born in Marosvásárhely, he became gendarmerie commander of Sopron after the fall of the Soviet Republic. On 17 February 1920 officers of his detachment murdered Béla Somogyi and Béla Bacsó of Népszava as a warning to Horthy’s opponents, and at the regency vote in March his troops kept “order” in the National Assembly. In August 1921 he refused to evacuate Sopron, opening the way for the town to remain in Hungary. That October he and other legitimist officers urged King Charles to seize power and escorted his armoured trains towards Budapest, but were defeated at Budaörs; he was amnestied and pensioned off. In 1932 he founded the Hungarian National Fascist Party under joint leadership with Pál Prónay.

bio.en: Born in Sopron and trained at the cadet school and war college in Vienna, he was the younger brother of the composer Ferenc Lehár. His First World War service won him the Knight’s Cross of the Military Order of Maria Theresa and a barony. During the Soviet Republic he raised a force of some 2,000 men in Graz, and in August 1919 he became military commander of Western Hungary, where his troops carried out reprisals against Communists and Social Democrats. A legitimist, he placed himself at King Charles’s disposal in March 1921 and was named defence minister in the second attempt that October; when it failed he fled through Czechoslovakia to Germany. He later lived in Berlin and Vienna, administered his brother’s estate, and died in Vienna in 1962.

epithet.en: Editor of the Social Democratic Népszava who was murdered by an officer detachment in 1920 for exposing the White Terror

bio.ko: 교사 출신으로 1903년부터 『네프서버』에 글을 쓰며 교사 조직 운동을 이끌었고, 1906년 헝가리 교사자유연합의 회장이 되었다. 카로이 미하이 연립정부에서 교육 담당 차관을 지냈으나, 평의회 공화국 때는 원칙적 이견 때문에 역할을 맡지 않고 평의회 전국대회에서 프롤레타리아 독재를 비판했다. 1919년 9월 『네프서버』의 책임 편집인이 되어 백색테러를 폭로하는 기사를 썼다. 1920년 2월 17일 오스텐부르크 부대의 장교들에게 동료 버초 벨러와 함께 끌려가 살해되었고 시신은 도나우강에 버려졌다. 1921년 호르티의 사면으로 가해자들은 끝내 처벌받지 않았다.
bio.en: A former schoolteacher, he wrote for Népszava from 1903, led the organisation of teachers, and in 1906 became president of the Free Association of Hungarian Teachers. He was state secretary for education in Mihály Károlyi’s coalition government, but during the Soviet Republic declined any role on grounds of principle and criticised the dictatorship of the proletariat in the National Assembly of Councils. In September 1919 he became responsible editor of Népszava and wrote articles exposing the White Terror. On 17 February 1920 officers of the Ostenburg detachment abducted and murdered him together with his colleague Béla Bacsó and threw the bodies into the Danube. Horthy’s amnesty of 1921 ensured the killers were never punished.

bio.en: Born in Mezőpetri, he left the Szatmár seminary after four years to become a journalist, edited the Christian Socialist Igaz Szó and the daily Új Lap, and was general secretary of the Catholic People’s Association from 1908 to 1918. After the fall of the Soviet Republic he was minister of propaganda in the Friedrich government and then, from November 1919 to December 1920, minister of religion and education. He prepared and tabled the numerus clausus bill, often seen as the first anti-Jewish act of twentieth-century Europe. He became chairman of the Christian National Union Party in 1920 but soon lost his seat, and by the time of his arrest in 1945 he was a textile merchant.

bio.en: A lawyer born into a Catholic professional family of Pécs, he was prefect of Baranya County from 1921 and of Somogy County from 1925. A close friend and ally of István Bethlen, he was interior minister in 1931–1935 and 1938–1944, directing the police against radical movements of both left and right, and in 1939 he banned the Hungarist movement. In 1941 he was the only minister to vote against declaring war on the Soviet Union, and he served briefly as acting prime minister after Teleki’s suicide and after Bárdossy’s resignation. Arrested by the Gestapo when Germany occupied Hungary in 1944, he was taken to Mauthausen, and he died of lung cancer in Vienna in 1948.

bio.en: Born in Budapest, he began his civil-service career in Pest County in 1909 and after the revolutions was head of Győr and Komárom counties. He entered parliament in 1927 and became Gömbös’s minister of agriculture in 1935. Succeeding Gömbös as prime minister in October 1936, he promised a return to Bethlen’s constitutional course and in 1937 banned the Party of National Will and had Szálasi imprisoned. In March 1938 he announced the Győr programme, but after the Anschluss he brought pro-German politicians into the cabinet and negotiated with the extreme right, and resigned in May. The First Jewish Law his government introduced passed under Imrédy, and from December 1938 until his death he was Speaker of the House of Representatives.

bio.ko: 형 앨프리드(뒷날 노스클리프 자작)와 함께 1896년 『데일리 메일』, 1903년 『데일리 미러』를 창간했고, 1922년 형이 죽은 뒤 어소시에이티드 뉴스페이퍼스의 지배권을 사들였다. 1914년 남작, 1919년 로더미어 자작이 되었고, 제1차 세계대전 중 한때 항공위원회 의장을 지냈다. 1927년 6월 21일 『데일리 메일』 사설 「헝가리의 양지」에서 트리아농 조약으로 잃은 영토의 상당 부분을 헝가리에 돌려주자고 주장해 헝가리의 국민 영웅이 되었고, 헝가리인 120만 명 이상이 감사 서한에 서명했다. 1930년대에는 히틀러를 찬양하고 1934년 영국 파시스트 연합을 지지했으며, 1940년 버뮤다에서 죽었다.
bio.en: With his elder brother Alfred, later Viscount Northcliffe, he founded the Daily Mail in 1896 and the Daily Mirror in 1903, and on his brother’s death in 1922 acquired his controlling interest in Associated Newspapers. Made Baron Rothermere in 1914 and Viscount Rothermere in 1919, he served for a time during the First World War as President of the Air Council. His Daily Mail editorial “Hungary’s Place in the Sun” of 21 June 1927 called for the return to Hungary of large territories lost under the Treaty of Trianon; he became a national hero in Hungary, and over 1.2 million Hungarians signed a letter of thanks. In the 1930s he praised Hitler and in 1934 backed the British Union of Fascists. He died in Bermuda in 1940.

bio.en: In November 1916 he succeeded his grand-uncle Franz Joseph as Emperor of Austria (as Charles I) and King of Hungary (as Charles IV). His secret peace negotiations with the Allies failed, and in the autumn of 1918 the empire fell apart. On 11 November in Austria and on 13 November in Hungary he renounced participation in affairs of state, carefully avoiding the word abdication. After going into exile in Switzerland in 1919, he twice tried to regain the Hungarian throne, in March and October 1921, but failed in the face of opposition from Regent Horthy. Arrested after the second attempt, he was exiled to the Portuguese island of Madeira, where he died of respiratory failure in 1922. The Catholic Church beatified him in 2004.

bio.en: Born Dimitrije Stojaković into a Serb family in Versec (Vršac), he served in the First World War as an intelligence officer of the Austro-Hungarian general staff. After the war he specialised in counter-espionage in Horthy’s counter-revolutionary army, was military attaché in Berlin from 1927 to 1933 and, from 1935 to 1944, Hungary’s minister in Berlin, where he pressed for alliance with Germany. Prime minister and foreign minister after the German occupation of March 1944, he legalised the Arrow Cross, dissolved the trade unions, jailed opponents and sharply accelerated the deportation of Jews. Forced out by Horthy’s pressure in August, he was captured by American troops after the war, handed over to Hungary, sentenced to death by a People’s Tribunal and shot in 1946.

bio.en: Born into a Swabian family at Rezsőháza in the Banat (now Knićanin, Serbia), he became a cadet in Vienna in 1897 and served as an Austro-Hungarian officer in the First World War. In 1919 he commanded the I Corps of the Hungarian Soviet Republic’s Red Army before going over to Horthy’s National Army in June. Retired in 1936, he was recalled in 1938 as Chief of the General Staff and, with Defence Minister Károly Bartha, became the leading advocate of alliance with Germany. He oversaw the invasion and annexation of Carpatho-Ukraine in March 1939 and, after the Kassa bombing of June 1941, at once blamed the Soviet Union and urged an immediate declaration of war. He left the post of chief of staff in September 1941; arrested by Soviet forces in February 1945, he was taken to the USSR and died there in 1952.

bio.en: Born Ferenc Knaus (or Knauz) at Moson, he served as an Austro-Hungarian staff officer in the First World War and in 1934 took his mother’s surname, Szombathelyi. In 1941 he led the Carpathian Group in the invasion of the Soviet Union. That September he succeeded Werth as Chief of the General Staff, and in January 1942 he ordered General Feketehalmy-Czeydner to intervene in Bačka, an operation that grew into punitive raids on Serb villages and the Novi Sad massacre. In 1943 he opened the investigation and court martial of those responsible for the massacre, and with Kállay he led the contacts with the Western Allies. Removed after the German occupation of 1944, he was sentenced to life imprisonment by a People’s Court after the war, handed over to Yugoslavia and shot at Petrovaradin in 1946.

bio.en: Born Franz Zeidner into a Transylvanian Saxon family, he served as an artillery and staff officer in the Austro-Hungarian army in the First World War, and between the wars changed his surname to the more Magyar-sounding Feketehalmy-Czeydner. In August 1941 he became commander of the Fifth Corps at Szeged. In January 1942 Chief of Staff Szombathelyi sent him against the partisans in Bačka; villagers there were massacred on his orders, and he organised the Novi Sad massacre. Sentenced to fifteen years by a court martial in January 1944, he fled to Vienna with other convicted officers and volunteered for the SS. As deputy defence minister under the Arrow Cross he signed the death warrant of his critic Endre Bajcsy-Zsilinszky. After the war he was handed via Hungary to Yugoslavia and executed in November 1946.

bio.en: He was born at Szarvas. In 1923 he founded the Guardians of Race Party with Gömbös but drew away, forming the National Radical Party in 1930; in the 1930s he turned to speaking out against antisemitism. In 1939 he returned to parliament for the Independent Smallholders’ Party. Turning against the war in late 1941, he called in the Christmas issue of Népszava for an Independence Front to take Hungary out of the war and bring land reform and universal suffrage; in January 1942 he warned Bárdossy of the coming Novi Sad massacre and then denounced it in parliament as “a state-organized pogrom”. Wounded in a gunfight resisting arrest when the Germans occupied Hungary on 19 March 1944, he was freed in October and in November elected president of the Liberation Committee of the Hungarian National Uprising, but was arrested again and hanged at Sopronkőhida on 24 December.

bio.en: The son of a Greek Catholic priest in Carpathian Ruthenia, then part of Austria-Hungary, he studied at the Ungvár school of theology and at Budapest University and was ordained. In 1918 he became head of the Subcarpathian National Council, which in 1919 asked for the region to join Czechoslovakia. In 1925 he was elected to the parliament in Prague as leader of the Ruthenian National Christian Party, and in October 1938 he was appointed head of the government of the Subcarpathian Autonomous Region. On 15 March 1939 he became president of Carpatho-Ukraine, but the next day Hungary occupied and annexed the region; he fled to Prague and spent the war as a professor at the Ukrainian Free University. Arrested by the NKVD when the Soviet army took Prague in May 1945, he was taken to Moscow and died in Butyrka prison in July.

bio.en: The son of a textile factory owner in Hornberg in the Black Forest, he fought as an officer in the First World War. He joined the Nazi Party in 1929 and the SS in 1930, and from 1933 was police president and head of the political police in Brunswick. Chosen by Himmler in June 1941 as Higher SS and Police Leader for southern Russia and Ukraine, he controlled all Einsatzgruppen killings in his area and used his method in the mass shootings at Kamianets-Podilskyi (23,600 killed) and Babi Yar (33,771 killed). Moved to Ostland in November with orders to complete the extermination of Riga’s Jews, he watched over two days as 25,000 people were killed at Rumbula. Taken prisoner fighting the Red Army in April 1945, he was sentenced to death at the Riga trial and hanged in Riga on 3 February 1946.

bio.en: Born in Budapest, he graduated from the military technical academy at Mödling in 1904. After the fall of the Soviet Republic he joined Horthy’s National Army. Appointed defence minister by Imrédy in 1938, he kept the post until 1942; with Chief of Staff Werth he pressed for full participation in the invasion of Yugoslavia and for fighting on the Eastern Front, and after the Kassa bombing demanded an immediate declaration of war on the Soviets. In 1942 he removed the age limit for conscription into labour service battalions and in June announced in parliament that Jewishness would be defined in racial terms. Horthy forced him to resign in September 1942 over his excessive pro-German stance. After the war a military court stripped him of his rank; he emigrated to Venezuela and died in 1964 while visiting Linz, Austria.

bio.ko: 오늘날 슬로바키아에 속한 데아키의 슬로바키아계 지붕장이 집안에서 서푸체크 죄르지로 태어나, 1901년 판논헐머의 베네딕도회에 들어가 1908년 사제가 되었다. 1927년 비오 11세가 그를 에스테르곰 대주교에 임명하고 추기경으로 서임했으며, 수좌대주교로서 당연직 상원 의원이 되었다. 1939년 독일의 폴란드 침공 뒤 헝가리로 피란한 폴란드인을 위한 교회의 구호를 조직했고. 1944년 봄 개종 유대인을 이송에서 빼 달라고 요구했지만 사제·수도자에 대한 예외만 얻었고, 이송을 공개적으로 규탄하지 않았으며 6월 29일 사목 서한을 내지 않기로 했다. 화살십자당 살러시의 「민족 지도자」 취임을 불법으로 보아 선서식 참석을 거부했고, 1945년 3월 에스테르곰의 방공호에서 숨졌다.
bio.en: Born Szapucsek György into a roofer’s family of Slovak origin at Deáki, now in Slovakia, he joined the Benedictines at Pannonhalma in 1901 and was ordained in 1908. In 1927 Pius XI appointed him Archbishop of Esztergom and made him a cardinal, and as Prince Primate he sat in the upper house of parliament in his own right. After the German invasion of Poland in 1939 he organised Church aid for the Polish refugees in Hungary. In spring 1944 he sought to have Catholic converts exempted from deportation but won the exemption only for priests, monks and nuns; he made no public condemnation of the deportations and on 29 June decided against issuing a pastoral letter. He regarded Szálasi’s inauguration as “Leader of the Nation” as illegal and refused to attend his oath-taking, and died in an air-raid shelter in Esztergom in March 1945.

bio.ko: 독일 졸링겐의 칼뱅파 가정에서 태어나 1914년 가족을 따라 오스트리아로 옮겨 자랐고, 1932년 나치당과 친위대에 들어갔다. 1938년 빈에서 오스트리아 유대인의 이주를 조직했다. 1939년 12월 국가보안본부 IV B4과장이 되었고, 1942년 1월 반제 회의에 참석해 회의록을 작성했으며, 이후 그와 부하들이 유대인을 절멸 수용소로 보내는 이송을 맡았다. 1944년 3월 독일의 헝가리 점령 뒤 헝가리 유대인 이송을 지휘해, 7월 이송이 멈출 때까지 72만 5000명 가운데 43만 7000명이 이송되었다. 전후 미군에 붙잡혔다가 수용소에서 달아나 1950년 아르헨티나로 건너갔으나, 1960년 이스라엘 모사드에 납치되어 예루살렘에서 재판을 받고 1962년 교수형을 당했다.
bio.en: Born to a Calvinist family in Solingen, Germany, he grew up in Austria, where the family moved in 1914, and joined the Nazi Party and the SS in 1932. In 1938 he was posted to Vienna to organise Jewish emigration from Austria. Head of RSHA Sub-Department IV B4 from December 1939, he attended the Wannsee Conference in January 1942 and prepared its minutes, after which he and his staff were responsible for deporting Jews to the extermination camps. After Germany occupied Hungary in March 1944 he oversaw the deportation of Hungary’s Jews; by the time the transports stopped in July, 437,000 of its 725,000 Jews had been deported. Captured by US forces after the war, he escaped from a detention camp and reached Argentina in 1950, but in 1960 Israel’s Mossad abducted him; tried in Jerusalem, he was hanged in 1962.

The highly publicised Eichmann trial resulted in his conviction in Jerusalem, following which he was executed by hanging in 1962.
